answer: Practically, the chain should bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because timber only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, vertex is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any wander approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
